name: Gcore Cloud / Functions / GPU

modes.label: Virtual machine
modes.note: gcore.com/pricing/cloud (rendered 2026-09-28, research/raw/gcore_com_pricing_cloud.txt): Standard Instances Gen 0/1/2, Linux, dedicated vCPUs, EUR/h ex VAT converted at 1.1378 USD/EUR (ECB 2026-09-28). "Prices do not include VAT and vary by location"; "billing only for active instances", free egress. Gen 0 = older Xeon E3-E5. Boot disk volume billed separately (price not captured -> disk_gib 0 means none included).

modes.label: Functions
modes.note: Current public FaaS pricing is regional per GB-second: Warsaw €0.00000277; Hong Kong €0.00000305; Amsterdam €0.00000345; Darmstadt/London/Paris-2 €0.00000352; Dubai/São Paulo-2 €0.00000517. Prices exclude VAT. Functions charge for the duration of allocated pods; an idle pod shuts down after its configured timeout and shutdown can take up to one minute.

modes.label: GPU instance
modes.note: Virtual GPU H100 list remains €2.36/h for 1× (24 vCPU/232 GB/1250 GB), €4.73 for 2×, €9.45 for 4×, €18.91 for 8×, ex VAT. Pay only while powered on; shelving preserves IPs and volumes at zero compute cost, so retained ancillary resources may still be billed. Separate Everywhere Inference and bare-metal GPU catalogs are not represented by gpu.H100.

modes.label: CPU Optimized Gen 1/2, Linux and Windows
Memory Optimized Gen 1/2, Linux and Windows

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Pay as you go, prices ex VAT.

caveats: VM and Virtual-GPU prices from the rendered public price tables (2026-09-28), EUR ex VAT converted at the ECB 2026-09-28 rate 1.1378; prices vary by location. Boot/data volume price not captured (disk beyond 0 GiB unknown).
2023 FaaS price is historical, not current confirmed pricing.
Unknowns remain null, not free; VM and GPU regimes are ordinary self-serve instances (not alt); Functions stays alt.
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Global footprint; EU company or edge POP is not proof that a chosen runtime/snapshot stays in EU.
Billing granularity / minimum for VMs not captured (page: "billing only for active instances"); engine meters per second, which flatters short bursts. VM boot time not measured.

Functions mode is FaaS (Python/Go runtimes, "without the need to create virtual machines"): no Docker, nested virt or desktop. VM/GPU: no desktop image documented (Gcore docs have users install XFCE manually on Linux servers).

FaaS (functions mode) memory price varies by region, EUR per GB-second: Warsaw 0.00000277, Hong Kong 0.00000305, Amsterdam 0.00000345, Darmstadt/London/Paris-2 0.00000352, Dubai/Sao Paulo-2 0.00000517.
Managed Kubernetes: control plane free; worker nodes billed at the same price as virtual instances or bare metal.

fleet.notes: Cloud quota-change API exposes requested global/regional limits and request status. Default new-account instance/vCPU/GPU quotas, approval timing and verification not publicly established in reviewed evidence; API example numbers are not defaults.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshot Schedules automate snapshot creation for selected volumes on a recurring basis.
snapshot_auto.note: Standard IaaS VM: nothing is captured on stop/idle; boot and data volumes simply persist (persistent_disk). Only scheduled (cron/interval) volume snapshots with retention/max count exist.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures the full state of a volume at a point in time. Snapshots support backup and recovery, and boot volume snapshots can deploy new Virtual Machines.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Volume (disk) snapshots via portal, REST API, Terraform, Python/Go SDK; no memory. New VMs can be created from boot-volume snapshots; images can also be made for templating. Gcore recommends stopping the VM first for consistency; billed at full volume size.

harness_api.note: VM product has no agent-harness API. Separate product Gclaw (managed OpenClaw on a dedicated VM, EUR 5.99/mo Lite) is driven through a chat UI in the Customer Portal / Telegram / Discord; its coding-agent skill 'Delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, or Pi agents', but no documented external API to prompt/stream/resume it.

egress_allowlist.quote: A security group is a set of rules that controls incoming and outgoing network traffic for Virtual Machines. Rules define which traffic is allowed or blocked based on protocol, port, and source or destination address.
egress_allowlist.note: Security-group outbound rules by protocol/port/destination CIDR or security group; default SG allows all outbound ('By default, all outbound traffic is allowed. Add outbound rules only if specific destinations or protocols need to be restricted.'). Not available for Bare Metal (use iptables there). No hostname-level egress control found.

ingress_rules.quote: For Sources, specify the allowed sources for inbound traffic: IP with mask: Specify an IP address range in CIDR format (192.168.1.0/24).
ingress_rules.note: Security-group inbound rules (protocol, port, source CIDR or SG); default SG opens SSH 22 and RDP 3389 plus ICMP. VMs can also be private-network only (public IP via floating/reserved IP is optional); load balancers and WAAP available.

guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VMs with root; Gcore's own docs tell Bare Metal users to configure iptables/nftables at OS level.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy. Gcore Secrets Manager only holds TLS certificates for HTTPS load-balancer listeners; VM secrets go in via user-data/SSH. (Gclaw stores user API keys in the VM's OpenClaw config: 'API keys and tokens provided to the agent are stored in the VM configuration'.)

volume_attach.quote: More than one volume can be attached to a Virtual Machine. However, volumes can only be used in the same region where the VM is created.
volume_attach.note: Block volumes (High IOPS SSD, Standard, SSD Low-Latency), attach/detach/resize via portal, API, Terraform.

volume_shared.quote: The NFS protocol allows servers within a subnetwork to simultaneously read, write, and modify files on the file share, providing data consistency and facilitating team collaboration.
volume_shared.note: File Shares = managed NFS mounted by many VMs / Bare Metal / K8s pods (RWX); per-CIDR access rules with access_mode rw or ro. GPU Cloud has VAST NFS shares (always read/write). Billed per GB.

isolation.quote: Deploy KVM-based Virtual Servers in KVM-SSD and KVM-HIGHCPU-SSD configurations with guaranteed resource allocation, SSD storage, SSH access, and VNC console.
isolation.note: The reviewed Edge Cloud VM docs don't name the hypervisor explicitly, but Gcore's VM product line (Hosting Virtual Servers, and the OpenStack-style Edge Cloud VM with dedicated vCPUs, floating IPs, security groups, volumes) is KVM-based; a full VM, not a microVM/container.

image_oci.quote: Upload a custom image to Gcore Cloud via the Customer Portal, REST API, or Terraform for use with Virtual Instances, Bare Metal servers, and GPU clusters.
image_oci.note: Custom images are VM disk images (qcow2/raw), not OCI/Docker container images. OCI images exist for a separate product (Container Registry / CaaS / Managed Kubernetes / Everywhere Inference), not for booting the VM product itself.

docker_inside.quote: Enable root user permanently on Linux VMs by modifying the cloud-init configuration, or run commands with root privileges temporarily using sudo, sudo su, sudo -i, and sudo -s.
docker_inside.note: Full KVM Linux VM with root/sudo access; Docker can be installed by the customer like on any Linux server. Not a managed/preinstalled feature - derived from full VM + root access, no explicit 'Docker inside a Gcore VM' doc found.

nested_virt.quote: Cloud Virtual Machine Hosting Rent high-performance virtual machines across 30+ global regions.
nested_virt.note: No documentation mentions /dev/kvm or nested virtualization support on standard multi-tenant Cloud VMs; not offered as far as reviewed evidence shows.

browser.quote: Cloud Virtual Machines for every workload ... Standard Dedicated vCPUs, including free egress traffic and billing only for active instances.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - a generic IaaS VM/GPU/Functions product, not a managed browser/desktop offering.

computer_use.quote: Cloud Virtual Machines for every workload ... Standard Dedicated vCPUs, including free egress traffic and billing only for active instances.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no screenshot/click driving API for a desktop on this IaaS product.

anti_bot.quote: Cloud Virtual Machines for every workload ... Standard Dedicated vCPUs, including free egress traffic and billing only for active instances.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Gcore does sell 'Bot Management' but that is a WAAP feature to detect/block bots hitting a customer's site, the opposite of stealth for outbound agent traffic; it is not part of the VM/Functions/GPU product modeled here.

captcha_solving.quote: Cloud Virtual Machines for every workload ... Standard Dedicated vCPUs, including free egress traffic and billing only for active instances.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope of a generic VM/GPU/FaaS cloud.

egress_ip_type.quote: Reserve a public or private fixed IP address in Gcore Cloud via the Customer Portal, REST API, or Terraform, and use the port ID to assign it to a Virtual Machine, Bare Metal server, or Load Balancer.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard cloud/datacenter IPv4 addresses from Gcore's own network; no residential/mobile IP product.

ssh.quote: Connect to Gcore Virtual Machines running Linux via SSH using key pairs or password authentication, with security group configuration and remote session setup.

snapshot.quote: A snapshot captures the full state of a volume at a point in time. Snapshots support backup and recovery, and boot volume snapshots can deploy new Virtual Machines.
snapshot.note: Volume/disk snapshots only (portal, REST API, Terraform, Python/Go SDK); no memory-state snapshot. No automatic snapshot on stop - only on-demand or scheduled volume snapshots.

fork.quote: boot volume snapshots can deploy new Virtual Machines
fork.note: A new VM can be created from a boot-volume snapshot of an existing VM, which is a clone/fork mechanism (disk-only, no running-process state).

fork_running.quote: Gcore recommends stopping the VM first for consistency
fork_running.note: Docs recommend stopping the VM before snapshotting for consistency; no documented ability to clone a live running VM without impacting it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot captures the full state of a volume at a point in time.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots/clones are disk-volume only; no memory/process-state capture, so forked/cloned VMs do not resume running processes.

pause_resume.quote: You only pay for active instances, with no charges when your VM is stopped.
pause_resume.note: Stopping a VM halts compute billing (volumes/IPs still billed separately); the VM can later be started again.

wake_on_request.quote: Virtual Machines are charged from the moment of creation until they are completely stopped.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a manually stopped/started IaaS VM, not a serverless product that wakes on an inbound request; Functions/FaaS scales pods on demand but that is a different mode, not documented as 'wake a stopped machine'.

auto_stop_idle.note: No documentation of an automatic idle-timeout stop for standard VMs - they run until the customer stops them; only the separate Functions/FaaS mode auto-shuts-down idle pods after a configured timeout.

live_resize.quote: Monitor Virtual Machine performance via the Monitoring tab, covering CPU Utilization, RAM Utilization, Network Traffic, Network Packets, and Disk IOPS.
live_resize.note: No 'resize flavor without reboot' documentation was found for Virtual Machines; changing vCPU/RAM typically requires selecting a different, fixed size/flavor which is not documented as being live. Derived/medium confidence.

agent_harnesses.quote: Cloud Virtual Machine Hosting Rent high-performance virtual machines across 30+ global regions.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The Cloud VM/Functions/GPU product has no preinstalled coding-agent templates. Gcore's separate 'Gclaw' product runs OpenClaw and can delegate to Claude Code/Codex/Pi, but that is a distinct managed-agent product, not part of this card's modeled VM/Functions/GPU offering.

own_agent_api.quote: Create and launch a Gclaw AI assistant instance in the Gcore Customer Portal, access the chat interface, and manage instance settings including Restart, Backup, Restore, and Recreate operations.
own_agent_api.note: Gclaw's OpenClaw agent is driven through a chat UI (Customer Portal / Telegram / Discord), not a documented first-party API to prompt/stream/resume it; and Gclaw is a separate product from the Cloud VM/Functions/GPU line this card models.

mcp_server.quote: Deploy Gcore MCP Server to expose CDN, Cloud, DNS, FastEdge, IAM, Security, Storage, Streaming, and WAAP operations as AI tools via Model Context Protocol.
mcp_server.note: MCP Server exposes Cloud compute/storage/networking (350 tools per the products-and-tools reference), which includes controlling Virtual Machines/instances.

lang_python.quote: Create FaaS functions in .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, and Python runtimes with code examples for basic handlers, dependency management via .csproj/go.mod/pom.xml/package.json/requirements.txt, and request/response object access through event parameters.
lang_python.note: Provided via the Functions (FaaS) mode, one of the card's modeled product modes; VMs are generic Linux images where Python isn't guaranteed preinstalled, but the FaaS runtime is a first-party out-of-the-box Python runtime.

lang_node.quote: Create FaaS functions in .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, and Python runtimes with code examples for basic handlers, dependency management via .csproj/go.mod/pom.xml/package.json/requirements.txt, and request/response object access through event parameters.
lang_node.note: Provided via the Functions (FaaS) mode as a first-party out-of-the-box Node.js runtime.

inbound_https.quote: Floating IPs Easily disable and migrate public IPv4 addresses between resources as needed.
inbound_https.note: VMs get a public IPv4 (floating IP); customers can run/terminate their own HTTPS server on it, and Gcore's Load Balancer product can also terminate TLS in front of instances. No managed 'HTTPS URL per port' proxy is documented, hence medium confidence.

egress_http_rules.quote: A security group is a set of rules that controls incoming and outgoing network traffic for Virtual Machines. Rules define which traffic is allowed or blocked based on protocol, port, and source or destination address.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: security group egress rules operate at protocol/port/CIDR (L3/L4) level only; no HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Reserve a public or private fixed IP address in Gcore Cloud via the Customer Portal, REST API, or Terraform, and use the port ID to assign it to a Virtual Machine, Bare Metal server, or Load Balancer.
static_egress_ip.note: A reserved/floating IP assigned to a VM is used for both inbound and outbound NAT (standard OpenStack floating-IP behavior), giving the instance a fixed outbound address; not explicitly documented as an 'egress IP' feature, hence medium confidence.

macos.quote: What types of virtual machines does Gcore offer? Gcore provides a range of virtual machines to suit diverse workloads, including Basic VMs with shared compute resources and dedicated options like Standard, CPU-Optimized, Memory-Optimized, and High-Frequency.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Gcore VM/GPU offerings are Linux and Windows only; no macOS instance type is documented anywhere in the Cloud, GPU, or Hosting product lines.

self_host.quote: Cloud Virtual Machine Hosting Rent high-performance virtual machines across 30+ global regions.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Gcore Cloud is a hyperscaler-run managed service; no documentation for running the platform on the customer's own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Cloud Virtual Machine Hosting Rent high-performance virtual machines across 30+ global regions.
byoc.note: not offered: no documentation of deploying Gcore-managed Cloud/VM infrastructure into a customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: Cloud Virtual Machine Hosting Rent high-performance virtual machines across 30+ global regions.
open_source.note: Gcore Cloud/VM/Functions/GPU is a proprietary managed platform; no OSI-licensed core product (SDKs/CLI tools may be open source, but not the platform itself).

soc2.quote: Our multi-level information protection infrastructure is ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certified and compliant with PCI DCC and GDPR. ... Gcore holds key certifications ... PCI DSS ... ISO 27001 ... GDPR
soc2.note: Gcore's compliance page lists ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and GDPR; SOC 2 is not mentioned anywhere in reviewed docs/marketing.

hipaa.quote: Gcore holds key certifications and adheres to international standards to ensure the highest level of security and data protection: PCI DSS ... ISO 27001 ... GDPR
hipaa.note: No mention of HIPAA eligibility or a BAA anywhere in reviewed Gcore compliance/marketing pages.

sso.quote: SSO accounts authenticated through Microsoft, Google, or GitHub cannot reset a password by email.
sso.note: Only social login via Microsoft/Google/GitHub OAuth plus 2FA is documented for the Customer Portal; no documented SAML/OIDC enterprise single sign-on for organizations.

eu_data_residency.quote: Data sovereignty and compliance Meet GDPR, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS standards by keeping data in-region with secure cloud locations.
eu_data_residency.note: Gcore explicitly offers keeping data in-region (including EU cloud regions such as Luxembourg, Poland) to meet GDPR.

max_session_h.quote: Virtual Machines are charged from the moment of creation until they are completely stopped.
max_session_h.note: Standard IaaS VM with no maximum runtime - it runs until the customer stops it (subject to payment/suspension rules).

desktop.quote: The VNC console in the Gcore Customer Portal provides browser-based access to a Virtual Machine (VM) without requiring internet access on the VM ... Both Windows and Linux VMs are supported. ... The VM connection is established. [image alt: "Windows desktop after connecting to the VM"]
desktop.note: reviewed: proposed correction rejected (Gcore's Customer Portal ships a built-in browser VNC console (Cloud > Virtual Instances > Access to Console) reachable for every Windows VM, and it shows the full graphical Windows desktop (screenshot alt text literally 'Windows desktop after connecting to the VM'), matching the desktop field definition (a graphical desktop via VNC/RDP/stream). This is a first-party, always-available feature of the VM product (not a separate paid add-on), so the top-level card claim desktop:false is incorrect for the VM/Windows product line. (For Linux VMs the same VNC console only shows a text login/serial console, not a graphical desktop, and the separate FaaS 'functions' mode has no desktop at all -- that sub-claim stays false.))

cpu_class.quote: Standard Dedicated vCPUs ... CPU-Optimized Dedicated vCPUs ... Memory-Optimized Dedicated vCPUs ... High-Frequency Dedicated vCPUs ... GPU Dedicated compute resources with state-of-the-art GPUs. / FAQ: 'Gcore provides a range of virtual machines to suit diverse workloads, including Basic VMs with shared compute resources and dedicated options like Standard, CPU-Optimized, Memory-Optimized, and High-Frequency.' / 'Gcore VMs offer dedicated vCPUs rather than shared cores, meaning your workload isn't competing for CPU time with other users.'
cpu_class.note: gcore.com/cloud/virtual-machines and gcore.com/pricing/cloud explicitly label the Standard (vm), CPU-Optimized, Memory-Optimized, High-Frequency and GPU product lines as having dedicated vCPUs/compute (as opposed to Gcore's separate 'Basic VM' shared_g1s/g2s line, which is not one of this card's modeled modes). windows-vm reuses the same Standard/CPU/Memory/High-Frequency families (g0w/g1w/g2w/g3aw flavors) with Windows licensing added, so it inherits the same dedicated-vCPU model (medium confidence, no separate Windows-specific dedicated statement found). arm64 (Ampere Altra a1-standard/-cpu/-memory flavors) is billed through the same 'standard/cpu/memory' pricing tables and flavor-naming convention as the dedicated x86 families, so it is treated as dedicated too (medium confidence; the Arm line is not individually named in the dedicated-vs-shared FAQ). bare-metal-gpu is a physical bare-metal server rented whole by one customer, so its cores are dedicated by definition (medium confidence, derived from 'bare metal' product description; no explicit vCPU wording since there is no virtualization layer). functions (FaaS) is serverless: Gcore's own docs describe Kubernetes pods with automatically allocated 'computing resources (CPU and memory)' that scale from 0 and share cluster nodes via K8s CPU requests/limits (mCPU), not a guaranteed dedicated core per function; graded 'shared' at medium confidence since no published CPU-share percentage was found. everywhere-inference (GPU-hour inference) is intentionally omitted: it is billed per-GPU-hour with no published vCPU allocation figures, so no cpu_class evidence was found for that mode.

usage_api.quote: Cloud resource usage and associated costs are available on the Cost reports pages in the Gcore Customer Portal. Reports are also available via the API. Each row shows the resource name, flavor, region, project, tags, usage, and cost.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; Cost Reports API provides per-resource billable usage data including individual VM costs. Filterable by project, region, resource type, and custom date ranges. Returns usage metrics and costs in EUR/USD for each Cloud resource.
